content: {"summary":"The orders‑api pods exhausted their own connection pools at 10:15 UTC on 8 August 2026 despite the orders‑db having ample slots. Each pod’s pool is limited to 25 connections (75 total), and a slow query kept those connections occupied, filling the pools and causing ORD‑5003 errors until the issue cleared at 10:40.","likely_cause":"A slow database query held connections open, filling the limited per‑pod pools and causing exhaustion despite sufficient database capacity.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Each orders‑api pod is limited to 25 connections, giving a total pool capacity of 75, far below the database’s 300‑connection limit.","evidence_ids":["INC-0182#1"],"quote":"orders-api runs three pods with 25 connections each, so its pools together reach 75 at most, and orders-db allows 300 connections."},{"text":"The exhaustion was due to connections being held too long, not a shortage of available database slots.","evidence_ids":["INC-0182#1"],"quote":"The trouble sat in how long each connection was held, not in how many could be opened."},{"text":"Pool usage hit the 25‑connection ceiling on the pods before requests began failing with ORD‑5003.","evidence_ids":["INC-0182#1"],"quote":"Pool usage on the two pods rose to its ceiling of 25 first. Only after that did requests start failing with `ORD-5003`."},{"text":"The incident lasted from 10:15 to 10:40 UTC, a 25‑minute window.","evidence_ids":["INC-0182#1"],"quote":"From 10:15 to 10:40, which is 25 minutes."}],"next_checks":["Identify the slow query in database statistics and measure its execution time","Add monitoring of pool usage with alerts before reaching the ceiling","Review and possibly increase per‑pod pool size or implement connection timeout settings","Confirm no other services are consuming unexpected connections during similar windows"]}
